title: Momentum and its conservation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Mechanics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: D09-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; D09-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; D09-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; D09-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D09-1#N.2, D09-1#N.5, D09-1#N.7, D09-1#N.10b, D09-1#N.16b.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Momentum
items.clue: Vector equal to mass × velocity, measured in kg m s⁻¹.

items.label: Newton's third law
items.clue: Reason two colliding bodies push each other with equal and opposite forces.

items.label: Explosion
items.clue: Event in which parts start at rest and move off in opposite directions, total p staying zero.

items.label: Kinetic energy
items.clue: Scalar that increases when a spring pushes two blocks apart from rest, though total p stays zero.

questions.stem: A baseball of mass m moving horizontally with speed v is struck by a bat. It leaves the bat moving horizontally with speed 3v/2 in the opposite direction. Taking the ball's initial direction of motion as positive, what is the change in the ball's momentum?

Two carts collide on a level track. Friction and air resistance are negligible. During the collision, Earth exerts a gravitational force and the track exerts a normal force on each cart. Is the total momentum of the two-cart system constant during the collision?

options.text: Yes, because Earth's and the track's forces are internal.
No, because the carts exert large forces on each other.
Yes, because the external forces on the system add up to zero.
No, because each cart's velocity changes in the collision.

questions.stem: Two blocks, of masses 1.0 kg and 4.0 kg, are held at rest on a horizontal surface with negligible friction, with a compressed spring between them. When they are released, the 1.0 kg block moves off at 2.0 m s⁻¹. Which statement about the 4.0 kg block is correct?

options.text: It moves off at 2.0 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It moves off at 0.50 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It moves off at 8.0 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It stays at rest, as the total momentum must stay zero.

questions.explanation: Total momentum starts at zero and stays zero: 4.0 × v = 1.0 × 2.0, so v = 0.50 m s⁻¹, opposite to the 1.0 kg block.

questions.stem: A 0.50 kg cart moving at 5.0 m/s collides with a 3.0 kg cart at rest on a level track with negligible friction. After the collision, the 0.50 kg cart moves backward at 1.0 m/s and the 3.0 kg cart moves forward at 1.0 m/s. How much of the system's kinetic energy is transformed into other forms of energy?

A skater of mass M stands at rest on level ice, where friction is negligible, and throws a ball of mass m horizontally with speed v relative to the ice. Which expression gives the skater's velocity immediately after the throw?

options.text: v, in the direction opposite to the ball
mv/M, in the direction opposite to the ball
Zero, since the skater remains at rest
mv/(M + m), in the direction opposite to the ball

questions.explanation: Total momentum starts at zero, and the throw forces are internal. After the throw, mv + M × (skater's velocity) = 0, so the skater moves back at mv/M, more slowly than the ball because M > m.
